cases.spec: unique(values) returns the first occurrence of every hashable value in input order; empty input returns []. Do not mutate the input.
cases.check:
from solution import unique
assert unique([3,1,3,2,1]) == [3,1,2]
assert unique(['z','a','z']) == ['z','a']
assert unique([]) == []
x=[4,2,4]; unique(x); assert x==[4,2,4]

cases.spec: records(text) parses standard CSV with comma separators and double quote escaping. Quoted commas and embedded newlines are legal. Return a list of lists of strings. Empty text returns []. Use the Python standard library.
cases.source:
def records(text):
    return [line.split(',') for line in text.splitlines()]
cases.check:
from solution import records
assert records('a,"b,c"
"x
y",z
') == [['a','b,c'],['x
y','z']]
assert records('"a""b",
') == [['a"b','']]
assert records('') == []
assert records('a,b
c,d
') == [['a','b'],['c','d']]

cases.spec: normalize(path) canonicalizes a relative POSIX path: discard empty and dot components; each .. pops one prior component. A leading slash or .. escaping above the root raises ValueError. The empty canonical path is "". Never touch the real filesystem.
cases.source:
def normalize(path):
    return '/'.join(p for p in path.split('/') if p and p != '.')

cases.spec: rolling(values, width) returns one mean for each complete consecutive window of positive integer width. Width larger than input gives []. Width <=0 raises ValueError. Do not mutate values. Values are real numbers.
cases.source:
def rolling(values, width):
    return [sum(values[i:i+width])/width for i in range(len(values))]

cases.spec: select(jobs) receives (start,end,profit) integer tuples with end>start and profit>=0. Return the ascending tuple of original input indices of a non-overlapping subset maximizing total profit. Half-open jobs may touch at endpoints. If profits tie, choose the lexicographically smallest ascending tuple (including empty tuple). Invalid jobs raise ValueError. Do not mutate input. Handle 1200 jobs without enumerating subsets. Deterministic ties must work with zero-profit jobs.

Decoder.feed(chunk) consumes arbitrary byte chunks of a framed stream: unsigned 4-byte big-endian payload byte length, followed by a strict UTF-8 string. Return all newly completed strings, buffering incomplete headers/payloads. Payload maximum 64 bytes, zero-length payload allowed. feed may receive multiple frames or partial UTF-8. finish() returns None only on a complete stream, otherwise raises ValueError. Invalid UTF-8 or oversized length raises ValueError and permanently poisons decoder. Once finish succeeds, later feed/finish raises ValueError. No data loss between chunks.

order(nodes, edges) returns a deterministic topological ordering. Nodes are distinct hashable strings in caller order. Edges are (before,after) pairs; duplicate edges are ignored. Repeatedly choose the currently ready node with smallest index in the ORIGINAL nodes input. This differs from merely sorting the final output or a depth-first walk. Cycles, duplicate nodes and edges referencing unknown nodes raise ValueError. Do not mutate input. Disconnected graphs and self-loops must work.
cases.check:
from solution import order
import random
assert order(['a','b','c','d'],[('d','a')])==['b','c','d','a']
assert order(['a','b','c'],[('a','b'),('a','b')])==['a','b','c']
assert order([],[])==[]
for nodes,edges in [(['a','b'],[('a','b'),('b','a')]),(['a'],[('a','a')]),(['a','a'],[]),(['a'],[('z','a')])]:
    try: order(nodes,edges)
    except (ValueError,): pass
    else: raise AssertionError((nodes,edges))
r=random.Random(983)
for _ in range(100):
    nodes=list('abcdefgh'); r.shuffle(nodes)
    topo=list(nodes);r.shuffle(topo)
    edges=[(a,b) for i,a in enumerate(topo) for b in topo[i+1:] if r.random()<.25]
    expected=[]
    while len(expected)<len(nodes):
        ready=[n for n in nodes if n not in expected and all(a in expected for a,b in edges if b==n)]
        expected.append(ready[0])
    nc=list(nodes);ec=list(edges); assert order(nodes,edges)==expected
    assert nodes==nc and edges==ec

cases.spec: paint(spans) takes (start,end,value) integer half-open intervals, in application order. Later intervals overwrite earlier ones. Return sorted disjoint (start,end,value) segments covering exactly painted points, merging adjacent segments with equal values. Gaps are not painted. Zero-length spans are ignored, reversed spans raise ValueError. Values may be None or unhashable lists, and None is a real paint value. Do not mutate input. Boundaries can be arbitrarily far apart, so never enumerate integer points between boundaries.
